segments.text: Welcome back to GitHub awesome. This is GitHub trending skills number four. 35 open- source skills trending on GitHub right now. Let's get into it.
AI Builder Club skills turns an ordinary repository into an agent ready loop system. Instead of leaving every coding
session to rediscover how to run, test, and prove a change, you've got agents making patches but no reliable local
stack, endto-end gate, or evidence that the app works. Its codebase harness scaffolds those checks. Isolated work
trees keep changes separate. And its loop skill builds a shared file-based knowledge base that agents continue from.
Self-learning skills is a meta skill that teaches your agent to recognize when it just earned a hard one golden path and save it where the tool
autoloads it next time. A new skill file, a cursor rule, an agent's MD entry, whatever fits. It captures dead
ends, too, since knowing what not to try again is worth as much as the win. It triages what's worth keeping so your config doesn't bloat with oneliners.
Adding custom skills to your coding agents is great, but when they randomly break across clawed code or cursor, you're stuck debugging cryptic sim links
by hand. Lazy Skills is an open- source terminal UI that centralizes your agent skills into a single mission control. It
automatically maps your setups, showing you exactly what each bot sees. It catches dead SIM links and lets you safely preview actions before running updates.
Hand auditing your code base for security bugs takes forever. And basic static scanners throw so many false positives that you don't even bother reading them.
Security audit skill is an open-source coding agent skill by Cloudflare that automates multi-phase repository security reviews. It coordinates
parallel agents to simulate attacks and cross-examine findings, delivering verified results without the noise.
Agent written code usually fails in the same boring ways. Fake APIs, useless tests, overbuilt abstractions, and docs that promise things the code never does.
Guard skills gives agents second pass review gates instead of more vibes. It includes clean code, test, docs,
WordPress, and WooCommerce guards, all as inspectable markdown skills. Let the agent build, then run the guard before you commit.
Shared agent skills sound tidy until every repo has a slightly different copied skill. MD aging in a corner.
Openclaw agent skills gives teams one canonical place for reusable coding agent workflows. It includes skills for redacted transcript provenence,
structured autoreview, remote validation, handoff prompts, and local session viewing, plus installer and validator scripts.
Prompt writing gets messy when every instruction is a list of things the model should avoid. Directional prompting gives agents a cleaner
pattern. Name the outcome first, then write every instruction as a forward action. It's a two-layer skill for prompts, agent directives, slash
commands, and skill MD files with the same directory structure working in claude code and codec cli.
Using AI agents for game development is great, but having to reexplain your engine context and saving systems in
every single session gets old fast, and you don't want to manage them manually.
Awesome. GameDev Agent Skills is an open- source library of 66 skills linked by a master router. It runs on cloud
code or cursor, automatically loading exactly what it needs for your active files. Multi-agent workflows get messy fast.
One agent plans, another edits, then nobody knows what was verified. Danny Mac 180's skills repo is tiny, but the
idea is specific. Its codec dynamic workflow skill helps codeex plan supervised AI agent work with goal mode, sub aents, or simulated work packets,
approval gates, integration, verification, and reusable workflow artifacts.
Architecture diagrams are static or need a browser to animate. Lancho makes premium black canvas handdrawn ones that move glow tracing the flow modules
pulsing from one JSON spec. It renders fully locally in Python and Pillow. No browser or cloud outputting an editable
Dexclad draw PNG and GIF. A verify flag frame diffs the GIF to prove it moves.
Agent skills are useful, but most examples still feel like internal demos you can't reuse. Hyper agent public
skills is a free pack of readymade creative and business workflows from the hyper agent team. The repo ships JSON skills for air table work tracking,
brand books, briefing trailers, claimation explainers, fashion editorials, data visualizations, small business websites, and design system work.
Paper rebuttals are where researchers suddenly become project managers, lawyers, and diplomats at the same time.
Awesome rebuttal turns that chaos into an agent skill. It builds local rebuttal memory, normalizes reviewer concerns,
plans experiments, drafts venue aware responses, and runs safety gates for unsupported claims, anonymity leaks, hostile tone, and fake numbers.
Most tighten this up tools hand you a rewrite and you just trust it. Plain writing skill is a set of plain text rules any agent can read, and it does
one thing the others don't. It shows its work as it strips anything that isn't pulling weight. It writes an HTML file with three tabs. First draft, second
draft, and a diff. Cuts are red, rewrites green, and the reason for each change shows on hover.
Multi-agent coding sounds efficient until two workers edit the same file and the main agent just believes whoever sounded confident. Edict agent turns
that into a governed codeex workflow. It starts with a chushi pre-flight, splits work into non-over overlapping slices,
assigns workers, reviewers, explorers, or verifiers, then forces the main agent to audit evidence, inspect diffs, run checks, and own the final answer.
Delegating code to another agent sounds productive, right up until it commits something you didn't review.
Delegate skills keeps the power dynamic sane. The orchestrator writes a self-contained brief, dispatches codecs through a small relay script, waits for
a structured result, reviews the diff, reruns the project gates, and lands the commit manually. Codeex implements in the background, but you stay the reviewer.
Research agents get dangerous when write the paper means one giant prompt with no ownership. CCFA skills breaks CCFA
paperwork into 15 staged roles. idea shaping, idea review, writing, scientific review, integrity audit,
submission checks, and rebuttal. The key object is CCFA, YAML, a shared project state file that keeps claims and revision ledgers from overwriting each
other. Staring at a massive folder of markdown notes, it's easy to lose track of how your ideas connect, so you don't
know where to find things. Brain map skill is an open source agent skill that compiles your Obsidian vault into an
interactive HTML map. It generates a themed forced directed graph with an animated timeline you can scrub to watch your base grow over time.
Most AI tutors just hand you the answer or spit out copypaste code blocks, leaving you with zero actual comprehension of the concepts.
Claude-Tutors is an open- source collection of Claude code skills designed to build genuine understanding.
Instead of giving away answers, it's designed to guide you socratically with dedicated skills for math and programming that help you master mental execution models.
Financial agents sound useful until they start guessing where the data came from.
Gaus 344/skills gives them named market data skills instead. Fred, C filings, Yahoo Finance,
and a long list of global and Argentina specific sources. It also includes tools for option pricing, back testing, and portfolio construction. Install only the
skill you need, then let the agent pull from that source.
Agent work is hard to learn from when all you keep is the final answer. For trace skill records, the process, task, context, tools, steps, observations,
retries, feedback, artifacts, and outcome. It ships a public trace schema, examples across science, legal, product,
and optimization workflows, plus scripts to validate traces and export JSON L.
Turn completed agent work into inspectable training material.
Every time you start a new Claude code session, your agent wastes a mountain of tokens relearning your entire code base.
Filitry skill is an open- source plugin that maintains a single markdown file with a oneline description for every file. It uses content hashes so those
summaries don't silently go stale, letting the agent grasp your layout in just a few hundred tokens.
A vague research idea can sound promising for months and still collapse the second you write the proposal. Good
question is an agent skill that forces the question to earn its keep. It takes a direction, literature gap or draft
proposal, then turns it into cards with stakes, rival explanations, falsifiers, a two-eek pilot, and the reviewer objection most likely to hurt.
You've probably seen dozens of prompts promising to make Claude Opus behave like Fable, only to realize most are just wish lists that don't work.
Fableize is an open-source Claude code plugin that makes Opus see tasks through to the end. Built on actual AB testing,
it enforces strict completion and verification steps as hard procedures so your model reaches its actual performance ceiling.
Moving from a raw concept to a deployed self-improving AI agent usually requires weeks of writing custom integration pipelines and configuring.
Launch your agent is a clawed code skill by Anthropic that automates this journey in your terminal. It interviews you about your goals and deploys the agent directly as a clawed managed agent.
Grading and scheduling runs so you don't have to manage infrastructure.
Brand work usually gets scattered across naming docs, audience notes, ad plans, and one forgotten tone guide. Brand building skills turns that into a set of
agent skills with shared context. You start with brand context, then branch into strategy, naming, identity, voice,
positioning, launch, ads, email, and more. Each skill reads the same brand DNA instead of guessing from scratch.
As your custom coding agent skills grow and iterate, your skill.md files quickly turn into bloated monolithic walls of pros that are impossible to maintain.
Functional Skill Creator is an open-source tool that breaks those long text prompts into modular testable functions. It isolates step logic and
generates unit tests so your agent pipelines don't silently regress.
Agent skills get messy when every workflow carries its own taste, rules, and half-remembered process.
DMroy/skills is a compact toolkit for Typescript teams that keeps those pieces separated.
Coding standards holds the design rules and architecture skills route into it instead of duplicating guidance. It also vendors Matt PCO's grilling and TDD
skills so reviews, specs, and refactors stay evidence-driven and deliberate.
AI image edits often fail in the same boring way. Glossy faces, centered framing, neon color, and zero restraint.
ANA image to image skill is a bilingual codec skill for pushing imageto image outputs toward a quieter cinema still look. It gives codec aterna inspired
color guidance composition rules negative constraints l workflow notes and three modes standard clean cinema and bleach bypass.
When you are vibe coding with AI files change so quickly that crucial design decisions end up trapped inside your
chat history. Repo doc skills is an open-source agent skill that asks coding agents to maintain living documentation
as they work. It keeps your guides and progress logs updated, mapping out what is planned and what still needs verification so you don't lose track of your architecture.
Most agent skill packs break a goal into tasks. Dang skills break it into independently verifiable slices, the part that lets an agent run unattended.
pointed at a feature and it carves the unknowns into pieces that build and verify in isolation and re-slices when
the plan goes stale. Every slice passes code and visual review before the loop moves on. The author ran one goal for 40 hours unattended.
Ask an agent to build a 3.js game and it hands you a static scene of placeholder cubes and calls it AAA. This skill pack
won't let it. A director routes the work to gameplay and graphics specialists, then gates completion behind proof. It
has to run, pass browser and mobile checks, and clear a visual scorecard from live screenshots before it's called done.
Coding agents can build the feature, but have no eye for design. Janky animations, default fonts, cramped spacing, muddy colors. Jacob Krel, the
designer behind Interfaces Dev, packaged his own taste into agent skills that target exactly those weak spots. Point
your agent at your UI, and it fixes each one with a designer's judgment, not generic defaults. Install it with one
line into Clawed Code or any Skillsaware agent.
The hardest part of a new product isn't building it, it's finding the first 10 people who want it. Point this codec skill at your startup's URL and it finds
people already complaining in public about the exact problem you solve. Each prospect links to the original post
scored on fit and timing with a respectful opener drafted for you. It uses only public signals, no private
data, and never auto sends. Ask an AI a solid geometry problem and you get a wall of text, maybe a wrong number, and
no way to see the shape. Edgelab turns it into an interactive lesson page.
Worked steps left, a rotatable 3D model right. Both come from one exact Simpy computation, so the picture and the
answer can't disagree. Feed it text or a photo. It's a clawed code plugin or plain Python. No claw needed.
You wrote the paper in Lex, but the journal wants Word. Run it through Pandock and every citation collapses into dead text you can't refresh and
Zotterero can't touch it anymore. This skill converts latex to a polished Word doc, but keeps the citations alive.
Native Zotterero fields you can still refresh inside Word. It applies your own word styles, audits every citation key,
and checks it opens without a repair prompt.
[music]
